record.paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
record.context_brief: Replacing infeasible FOT with scenario simulation
record.original_question: How can automated-driving system verification avoid infeasible field operational testing, which may require hundreds of thousands to hundreds of billions of miles, by using simulation and short-mileage test-course reproduction of rare corner-case scenarios that have extremely low occurrence probability on actual roads?

evidence.quote: However, obtaining statistically significant results would require conducting FOT by driving for hundreds of thousands to hundreds of billions of miles FOT [11]. In order to verify the system within a realistic time-frame, it is necessary to accelerate the experiment by simulation, reproducing the corner-case scenarios on test courses with a short mileage, i.e., scenarios with extremely low probability of occurrence and difficult to statistically obtain (rare) by FOT on the actual road.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the verification of an automated-driving system whose safety claim requires statistically significant evidence of correct behavior across the operational domain. Direct field operational testing (FOT), in which the system is driven on public roads to accumulate exposure to real traffic, is estimated to require on the order of 10^5 to 10^11 miles to attain such statistical significance, which is infeasible within realistic project time-frames. A central source of difficulty is the existence of "corner-case" scenarios — situations whose probability of occurrence on actual roads is extremely low, so that they are essentially never sampled by FOT, yet whose correct handling is critical to the system's safety case.

Develop a verification methodology that replaces, or substantially reduces reliance on, infeasible FOT by combining:
(a) simulation-based testing, in which scenarios are generated and executed in a virtual environment, and
(b) short-mileage reproduction of rare corner-case scenarios on physical test courses.

The methodology must specify:
1. A formal definition of the operational domain and of the class of corner-case scenarios to be covered.
2. A procedure for systematically generating, sampling, or enumerating corner-case scenarios with extremely low natural occurrence probability so that statistically meaningful coverage is achieved.
3. A quantitative argument relating performance measured under simulation and short test-course mileage to the safety performance that would have been measured by full-scale FOT, including a treatment of the reality gap between simulated/test-course conditions and real-road conditions.
4. Criteria under which the combined simulation plus short-mileage test-course evidence is sufficient to substitute for FOT of the order required for statistical significance.

Provide such a methodology, or prove that no methodology meeting all four requirements can exist under stated assumptions.
artifact.status_search_result: The challenge of replacing infeasible field operational testing of automated driving systems with scenario-based simulation and short-mileage test-course reproduction of rare corner cases remains an active, unresolved research area. Standards efforts (ISO 21448 SOTIF, UL 4600) and ongoing scenario-based testing research (Pegasus, NHTSA frameworks, and numerous arXiv papers through the mid-2020s) continue to propose partial methods (scenario libraries, importance sampling, adversarial scenario generation, reality-gap quantification), but no generally accepted methodology provides a quantitative substitute for full-scale FOT.

status_evidence.title: ISO 21448 SOTIF and scenario-based testing
status_evidence.snippet: ISO 21448 addresses Safety of the Intended Functionality for road vehicles, including handling of unknown hazardous scenarios; the standard frames the problem but does not provide a closed quantitative substitute for FOT.
status_evidence.claim: Scenario-based verification methodology for AD systems is still being standardized and remains an open methodological problem.

status_evidence.title: PEGASUS Project — Scenario-based assessment of automated driving
status_evidence.snippet: The PEGASUS project developed scenario-based methods to reduce required test mileage but acknowledges open issues in coverage and statistical equivalence to FOT.
status_evidence.claim: Scenario-based simulation reduces but does not yet rigorously replace FOT for statistical safety assurance.
